root_cause.text: The AppArmor `unpack_pdb` function failed to validate that DFA start states extracted from untrusted policy data were within the bounds of the DFA state table before being used as array indices, causing an out-of-bounds memory read.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states "Start states are read from untrusted data and used as indexes into the DFA state tables... if the start state exceeds the number of states in the DFA, this results in an out-of-bound read," and the patch diff shows the addition of `if (pdb->start[0] >= state_count || pdb->start[AA_CLASS_FILE] >= state_count)` to reject invalid states.

intent_record.intent_summary: Adds boundary validation to prevent out-of-bounds access when unpacking AppArmor policy DFA start states
intent_record.what: Added bounds validation for DFA start state indices (pdb->start[0] and pdb->start[AA_CLASS_FILE]) against the total state count from the DFA tables, with early failure if values exceed valid range
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds array access when using start states later in execution by validating they are within the DFA's actual state count before proceeding with policy initialization
